ext.description: See which process holds a port, which VS Code window it belongs to, and free it safely. Detects EADDRINUSE with Kill & Retry, orphaned dev servers, and never kills the wrong project.
container.title: Who's On My Port
welcome.unsupported:
Who's On My Port supports Windows only in v1.0. macOS and Linux support is on the roadmap.
[Follow on GitHub](https://github.com/OAB710/whos-on-my-port)
cfg.sortBy: Order of ports inside each project (and in the flat list). Project order is not affected.
cfg.sortBy.name: Process name, A–Z.
cfg.groupByProject: Group ports by project. When off, ports are listed flat (Pinned stays on top).
welcome.empty:
No ports in use right now.
[Kill Port...](command:whosOnMyPort.killPort)
[Ports Reserved by Windows](command:whosOnMyPort.showReservedPorts)
[Settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22whosOnMyPort%22%5D)
cfg.liveRefresh: Keep the Ports view up to date in real time. Runs only while the view is visible and the window is focused: a cheap `netstat` check every few seconds, and a full scan only when ports open or close (plus every 30 s to refresh memory).
cfg.liveRefreshIntervalSeconds: How often (seconds) live refresh checks for opened/closed ports. Requires `#whosOnMyPort.liveRefresh#`.
cfg.confirmBeforeKill: Ask for confirmation before stopping a process.
cfg.filterDevOnly: Show only development processes (hide Windows system services).
cfg.customDevProcesses: Extra process names (without .exe) to treat as development processes.
cfg.gracefulStop: For processes running in a terminal of this window, send Ctrl+C first and force-kill only if the port is still busy.
cfg.gracefulTimeoutMs: How long to wait (ms) after Ctrl+C before force-killing.
cfg.detectPortInUse: Watch terminal output for 'port already in use' errors and offer Kill & Retry (requires terminal shell integration).
cfg.showStatusBar: Show the number of ports used by this workspace in the status bar.
cfg.pinnedPorts: Ports always shown at the top with their free/busy state. Pin/Unpin saves to your User settings; if you set this in a workspace's settings, that per-project value is used and updated instead.
cfg.memoryWarningMB: Mark processes using at least this much memory (MB) with a ▲ badge in the tree. `0` = off.
cfg.longRunningHours: Mark processes running for at least this many hours with a ⏱ badge in the tree. `0` = off.
cfg.history.enabled: Remember the terminal commands that opened a port in this workspace (*Port History…*) so you can run them again. Stored in VS Code's workspace storage, never in your project. Secrets in commands (`API_KEY=…`, `--token …`) are replaced by `***` before saving.
